'Target attack action card with Herald in its name gets +2{p}' -- the card's TYPE is Instant, and its ability is what happens when it is PLAYED -- so the ability_type is PLAY. Authored as ATTACK_REACTION first and then as INSTANT, and tests/test_ability_type_sweep.py rejected both: ATTACK_REACTION on a card that is not one never fires, and the INSTANT ability_type is for a card whose TEXT carries an 'Instant - ...' activated ability, which this one does not. Either way the card looks implemented and does nothing.

'WITH HERALD IN ITS NAME' IS A SUBSTRING, not a name. ATTACK_NAME_IN compared whole names (colour suffix stripped, so one entry covers all three printings) and no card is called 'Herald', so an exact comparison is false in every state -- silently, because a filter that matches nothing looks like a board with no legal target. `name_contains` is a separate key so a card naming ONE specific attack cannot start matching a family; 40 cards in the corpus use this templating.

The conditions gate the ability rather than targeting, because an Instant resolves while the attack is already on the chain: the 'target attack action card' it can reach IS the active attack. ATTACK_TYPE_IN Action keeps a weapon attack whose name contains Herald out.
